scenes.text: A customer clicks once. Your webhook arrives twice. Watch what breaks. This is Reflex, an engineering agent that learns from verified repairs.
The same operation creates two orders and deducts inventory twice. This is a sample incident, but the code is really running. We're showing saved, real execution results.
Two of four checks fail. Repeated deliveries must preserve the original outcome, while different orders must still work. That contract gives the agent a concrete target.
River generates this patch. It recognizes an existing operation before changing inventory, and returns its original response. The recorded checkout repair took about fifteen seconds.
The model produced code. Execution determined whether it worked. All four checks pass, including distinct operations and delayed retries. The repair and its evidence stay together.

River proposes repairs, execution verifies them, and only verified repairs train the model. This is rejection sampling fine tuning. Twenty four generated tasks led to twenty three River requests and nineteen verified repairs. With five accepted repairs, we trained on twenty four examples.
River completed sixteen weight updates and saved this checkpoint. The training snapshot preserves exactly which examples were used. The trained adapter can be downloaded from River Console.
All three passed our four held out failures. The set is too easy to show a gap, so we are not claiming one.
Teams should keep the intelligence their work creates. UFO has an SDK verified extension; River trains the specialist. Your failures become your dataset. Your dataset becomes your model.
